paras: On the bank of a wide river stood a tall jamun tree, heavy with sweet purple fruit. In it lived a cheerful monkey named Raktamukha. One day a tired crocodile climbed onto the bank to rest beneath the tree. The kind monkey tossed him a handful of jamuns. “Eat, friend,” he said. “They are the sweetest on this river.”

The crocodile, Karalamukha, loved the fruit. He came back the next day, and the day after that. Soon the two became the best of friends. They talked for hours, and every evening the crocodile carried jamuns home to his wife.

But the crocodile's wife was greedy. “If the fruit is this sweet,” she said, “imagine how sweet the heart of the monkey who eats it every day must be! Bring me his heart, or I will never speak to you again.”

The crocodile was troubled, but he could not refuse her. The next day he said to the monkey, “My wife wants to thank you. Come home with me for dinner. Sit on my back, and I will carry you across the river.”
The monkey happily jumped onto his back. But in the middle of the deep river, the crocodile began to sink. “Forgive me,” he said. “My wife wants to eat your heart.”

The monkey's heart pounded, but he kept calm. “Oh, my dear friend!” he laughed. “Why didn't you tell me before? We monkeys keep our hearts safe in the trees. Mine is hanging on the jamun tree. Take me back, and I will fetch it for your wife.”

The foolish crocodile turned around and swam back to the bank. The moment they reached the shore, the monkey leapt up to the highest branch. “You foolish creature!” he called down. “Can anyone keep his heart outside his body? You betrayed a true friend. Our friendship ends today.”
Ashamed, the crocodile slid away into the water.
Moral: Keep a calm mind in danger. Quick thinking can save you when strength cannot.
